posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
This one is a marathon, not a sprint. Here are some tips to help!

1. Gloomy typically does 3 damage. A construct can take a single hit, so prioritize which constructs get that hit. 

2. Unless you have a Cosmic Crest in play, you can use destructive reflex to ping your own constructs to activate them. 

3. The sable pins are just awful. I found that getting rid of them ASAP was extremely useful. 

4. Cursed Acolytes are a major threat, BUT you can prioritize their damage. I found that stacking wounding buffers on the Argent Adept was extremely useful as a counter to them, as was having them hit Dynamic Siphons to let Legacy charge motivationally. 

5. You want the Argent Adept to get an Inspiring Supertonic soon. Having Legacy be able to charge twice in a round is very useful, especially once you have some autonomous blades in play. 

6. Relics can be destroyed by the Adept. Since Gloomy can potentially use the book to destroy every construct in play (4 damage to all hero targets if no one discards), you need to consider VERY carefully if it is worth sacrificing an instrument. 

7. Once Gloomy flips, have a plan. He does 3 damage to all targets... which isn't enough to kill any constructs if you have them at full HP, but will activate all of them. So it can definitely be turned to your advantage if you stack siphons on Legacy. 

8. The Cosmic Crest makes Captain C. And all constructs immune to energy damage. Battalion gunners do Energy damage. Maybe you prefer being immune, maybe you prefer letting the gunners ping your siphons and vitality conduits.  Either way you choose it, think about how their damage will impact the health of your constructs on Gloomy's turn, since he does 3 damage. 

9. Remember that you can choose which target Gloomy hits if their are multiple ones that meet the criteria!  It can be REALLY useful to let a gunner or mechanic get punched, particularly if they are hiding behind a shield. 

Good luck!

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Comfortable Mint, but this one was interminable. No idea how many rounds it went - Sky Deck made it hard to tell, since I buried at least 5 of Gloomweaver's targets back under his deck. Because of Sky Deck, Gloomy never got the chance to reshuffle. I dodged the worst of Vast Following's potential. Among the Vast Followings, he pulled out all of one relic and one Cultist combined.
 
I normally hit Random and go, but there are a few matches I would outright reject. This fits one of my rejection criteria: "Legacy vs. Skinwalker Gloomweaver". Given a little bit of setup, Legacy can easily win by himself. I didn't get the "you win" setup, though, because I never saw Next Evolution.
 
That's OK - once I FINALLY got Argent Adept set up, this match got a whole lot easier. I had a lot of trouble getting going because AA kept having to play Relic wiper with Cedistic Dissonant. I blew up instruments four times in six turns to prevent Gloomy from getting too well set up. Unfortunately, that was at the cost of my own setup, and I ended up getting all three heroes knocked down below 10 HP by an ill-timed combo of Strength of the Grave / Chosen Disciple with two Zombies out, which laid down a pile of damage. Luckily we were able to string together enough hits to wipe that crew out in one round, leaving us to patch our health back up with a whole lot of uses of Motivational Charge.
 
When I finally got things the way I wanted them (Legacy with everything but Next Evolution, Dynamic Siphons on Legacy and Argent Adept, Augmented Ally on Argent Adept, and Cosmic Weapon on Captain Cosmic, AA wth several instruments and Ongoings to play with, and no setup for Gloomy), I started wailing on Gloomweaver to the tune of 49 damage in the first round after he flipped, after which he was down for the count within two more rounds. I abused the Battalion Gunners to give myself 4 power uses during the first environment turn after the flip, which sped the process significantly. A couple of Lead From the Front uses and/or Sustained Influences got mixed in there to keep the Dynamic Siphons alive. Argent Adept dealt the finishing blow from the Accompany on Syncopated Onslaught.
 
Finished with Legacy at 17 (after taking 8 in the last round from Gloomweaver via Lead From the Front), Captain Cosmic at 16, and as a cherry on the top of "screw you, Gloomweaver", Argent Adept at full HP.
 
On one hand, it was kind of annoying and took forever (per my iPad's battery meter in Settings, a shade over 2 hours), but on the other hand, I hadn't had a good Argent Adept Shenanigans match in a while, so at least running him was fun.

posts.cooked:
Mint.  Finally.  I didn't count rounds, but it took ~1.5 hours.  And most of that was clicking through mass damage.

 

It turns out that Legacy with Fortitude, Lead From the Front, and 3 Energy Bracers is nigh invulnerable.  (And Superhuman Durability can deal with the handful of things that Gloomy can do to deal 5+ damage.  But it takes FOREVER.

By the end I was killing off Cursed Acolytes, not because they were dangerous (actually, they were helpful, because they could trigger my Dynamic Syphons), but because they took too long to deal with.

 

At my nadir, all heroes were below 10 hp.  By the end, they were all above 20.

 

Jeysie:

The Sky Deck is a lovely card… Gloomy's Vast Followings just pulled out a zombie or two thanks to it.

Be careful, though.  I got stuck in a loop near the end where Gloomy's deck was almost entirely cultists and zombies, and they kept chaining.

posts.name: scifantasy
posts.cooked:
Fine. With which I was, ahem, fine. Went into the first game clueless (I haven't played against Gloomwalker Skinweaver much), and got swamped. Second game, I was still clueless, but spent more time trying to understand the flow of play. Got further, but not far enough. Braithwhite's tips up there, though, cracked the whole thing wide open. My heroes were all comfortably over 10 HP (in fact, I think the Alliterative Duo were over 20; and even Legacy was only where he was becasue of a fumbled Lead from the Front play) and the stack of Autonomous Dynamic Buffers (now available in your local store, from RevoCorp!) on Legacy meant I was healing 2-4 damage per target per round and dealing something like 20-30 damage.

Still, I didn't find it all that fun, I have to say. Not even because it was Gloomskin Walkerweaver, but--well, because I was on my phone, for one, and more specifically I was on my phone dealing with precise ordering of mass targets. If I hadn't already unlocked Termi-Nation Unity, this game might have done it all by itself. I needed more screen real estate to avoid spending all my time scrolling left to right and back.

(Something I may submit as a feature request to Handelabra: Sort by Character. Instead of the "Choose Target" menu going in chronological order of target, I'd rather see Legacy then everything attached to him, then all of CC's, then AA's, then Weaverskin Walkgloomer's, then the environment's. For example.)

Environment was mostly irrelevant, thanks to Bracers, the Cosmic Crest, and all three Shield Generators; Sky Deck did help me avoid recurring relics from Vast Followings though.

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
Arcanist Lupus:

Mint.  Finally.  I didn't count rounds, but it took ~1.5 hours.  And most of that was clicking through mass damage. It turns out that Legacy with Fortitude, Lead From the Front, and 3 Energy Bracers is nigh invulnerable.  (And Superhuman Durability can deal with the handful of things that Gloomy can do to deal 5+ damage.  But it takes FOREVER.

I went basically the same route, and took just about as long.  Near Mint (I screwed up one of AA's super-fiddly multiple instruments/power/card play turns and had to undo), but Flawless Victory – all heroes at max HP.  

 

Legacy was tanked to the max, with not only three Energy Bracers but also three Autonomous Blades, Surge of Strength, Inspiring Presence, and the Legacy Ring.  With all of the buffs and constructs, every Motivational Charge did at least 5+4+4+4=17 points of damage, and that's if I didn't have AA in there adding extra out-of-turn Galvanize uses.  

 

I can just imagine this playing out in the "real world":  

Gloomy's little cultists obtain one of Blade's old MDPs, and use it Renfield-style to transport the corpse of their dead master.  Using an unholy ritual, they raise him from the dead.  Our three heroes break into the MDP and try to clean out the nest of cultists, but they have to chase them through the labrynthine corridors of the MDP.  The cultists take full advantage to backstab, sneak attack, and place Gloomy's little voodoo pins all over the heroes, while the MDP crewmembers snipe and strafe from cover.  It's a long, ugly, bloody fight.  After finally clearing out the last of the cultists, our beat-up and weary heroes emerge on the flight deck, where they are greeted by the horrifying sight of a colossal demon zombie Gloomweaver, oozing malice and baleful magic. 

But here where they have room to move, the heroes' teamwork finally comes into play:   Every time the demon monster aims one of his tremendous fists at Legacy, an equally massive yellow energy shield from Captain Cosmic deflects the blow. At the same time, yellow energy swords are whirling in an arc around the enraged monster, darting and slicing.  All the while, the eerie long-haired stranger dressed in silver plays his otherwordly music, which, powered by the pure stellar energy flowing out of Captain Cosmic, is visible and tangible, as well as audible.  The music literally lifts and sustains the heroes:  It washes away the pain and weariness from the long fight in the corridors, their bruises visibly fade, open wounds stop bleeding and begin to knit themselves shut. They think more clearly, move more quickly, fight more creatively. 

Legacy begins to go on the offensive.  The music enhances even Legacy's own inherent super-speed.  He becomes a stellar energy-powered blur, barely visible.  At the same time, he's throwing cosmically- and musically-enhanced punches that could level buildings.  The resurrected Gloomweaver is puissant and terrible, but even this hellish revenant is simply no match for the onslaught of 200 years of enhanced human evolution, powered by cosmic energy and arcane melodies.  Gloomweaver goes down in a hail of lightning-fast blows and incandescent streaks of yellow energy, his cries of rage and despair drowned out by music that seems to be coming from everywhere and nowhere at the same time.
